sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints: bicyclists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and distracted driving

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
A bicyclist has two valid right-turn signals, right arm straight out or left arm bent up, so a raised left arm means right, not left. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty three; prereq sec14-F18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
A left arm bent downward means the rider is slowing or stopping, while a left arm held straight out means a left turn. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty two; confusable sec14-F18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
The stop-as-yield rule covers bicyclists aged 15 and up only, and only when the intersection is clear and they already have the right-of-way. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty three; prereq sec14-F06. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A01
Lane filtering is passing stopped traffic within a lane at low speed, and the rule is written for two-wheeled motorcycles. [A01]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A01
You may cross a bike lane to turn or to enter or leave a road, driveway or alley, but you may not block it. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F01. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians have the right-of-way at intersections and crosswalks even where no lines are painted. [A02]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F27. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A02
Hands-free use is allowed for mobile devices, but careless driving from texting or any manual device use can still bring a fine or misdemeanor charge. [A02]
Why it matters: group distraction; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F35. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A02
When turning on red, the checks come in order: stop and check for pedestrians in every direction first, then edge forward to look for vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F28. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0027]

Misconception: a mental distraction is safer than a hands-on one; it is just as dangerous. [A02]
Misconception: a quick honk warns a bicyclist safely; it can startle the rider into a crash. [A01]
Misconception: a motorcyclist weaving within a lane is driving carelessly; riders move in the lane to see, be seen and avoid hazards. [A01]
Misconception: you may pass a car stopped at a crosswalk if your lane is clear; it may be stopped for someone you cannot see. [A02]
Mnemonic: Reach across, look back: the Dutch Reach. [A01]
Mnemonic: Eyes, hands, mind: keep all three on driving. [A02]
Glossary: Dutch Reach means opening the car door with the hand nearest the center of the vehicle after checking for bicyclists. [A01]
Glossary: Conflict Zone means a marked road area that, where one exists, is the place to make a right turn from. [A01]
Glossary: Pedestrian means a person standing, walking, running or using a mobility aid on a road or private property. [A02]
Glossary: Aggressive driving means willful driving that endangers people or property without regard for safety. [A02]
